input: Schedule a termite inspection before listing the house

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The listing date sets a hard deadline that determines how urgently the inspection must be booked and how much buffer time exists for follow-up treatment if needed.
The property's location determines which licensed inspectors are available, regional regulations, and whether travel or access logistics are involved.
Knowing whether this is just a termite inspection or a broader wood-destroying organism or general pest inspection changes who to hire and what report is produced.
Whether the user already has an inspector in mind, needs a referral, or requires the real estate agent to arrange it changes the immediate next action.
Access to the property — whether it is owner-occupied, tenant-occupied, or vacant — affects scheduling, notice requirements, and who needs to be coordinated with.
Understanding what a good outcome looks like — a clean report, or a report plus treatment plan — shapes how results will be used in the listing process.
Budget range for the inspection affects which companies or tiers of service to consider, especially if the user also wants treatment options quoted at the same time.

gold.taskTitle: Schedule termite inspection before listing the house
gold.taskDescription: Arrange a professional termite inspection for a property in preparation for putting it on the real estate market.

questions.title: When do you plan to list the house?
questions.description: Identify the target listing date or timeframe to set the deadline for completing the inspection and any follow-up actions.

questions.title: What city or region is the property located in?
questions.description: Determine the property's location to identify available licensed inspectors and any local regulatory requirements.

questions.title: Should this cover only termites or all wood-destroying organisms?
questions.description: Clarify the scope of the inspection — termite-only vs. a broader pest or WDO report — to ensure the right type of inspector and report is arranged.

questions.title: Do you already have an inspector in mind to contact?
questions.description: Establish whether the user needs help finding and vetting an inspector, or simply needs a plan to contact one they already know.

questions.title: Is the property currently occupied, vacant, or tenant-occupied?
questions.description: Determine access logistics and whether advance notice to occupants or coordination with a property manager is required before scheduling.

questions.title: Do you need a clean report, or just findings before deciding next steps?
questions.description: Understand what success looks like — a report confirming no issues for the listing, or an assessment that may lead to treatment before listing.

questions.title: What is your budget for the inspection itself?
questions.description: Identify the budget range to filter inspection services appropriately, especially if same-visit treatment quotes are also desired.
